title: Curves and Text
summary: Add a text object, type into it in Edit Mode, give it depth with Extrude and Bevel, and extrude a Bézier curve's points.
expect: Text and Bezier curves are typed, edited, extruded and beveled as in Blender; the 3D Text demo's Google Fonts title needs network access.
limits: The 3D Text example builds its text from code with a Google Fonts family and needs network access; a text object added with Shift A uses Blender's built-in font.

title: Drivers and the Graph Editor
summary: Shape animation as F-curves in the Graph Editor, repeat or shake them with F-curve modifiers, and drive one property from others with drivers, here a steam engine whose flywheel moves everything else.
expect: F-curves, their modifiers and drivers are Blender's and evaluate as in Blender, simple expressions without Python; a driver's Python expression starts Python on first use, which takes a few seconds.
limits: A driver whose expression needs Python (anything Blender's simple expression evaluator does not take) waits until Python has started, a few seconds after its first use.
The example's drivers and modifiers are made by its script; the steps show them and change a key rather than build them from nothing.

title: Geometry Node Editor
summary: Show and edit the node group of the active Geometry Nodes modifier, here the Hair Dynamics example's Generate Hair Curves.
expect: Node groups open, edit and evaluate as in Blender; the sidebar's Group tab is missing, and Bylonder's own Geometry Nodes modifier opens in Babylon's editor instead.
limits: Bylonder's own Geometry Nodes modifier keeps its Babylon graph and opens in Babylon's Node Geometry Editor, not here.
The sidebar's Group tab (interface panels) is not shown yet; inputs are added from Group Input's empty socket.

title: Geometry Nodes
summary: Build a Geometry Nodes modifier from an empty node group, expose its inputs, make node groups, and see the evaluated mesh, points and instances drawn.
expect: Meshes, points and mesh instances evaluate and draw as in Blender; volumes and instanced curves are not drawn, and instances take their mesh's first material.
limits: Volumes are evaluated but not drawn; curves draw as the hair curves do.
Instances draw where their geometry is a mesh, an object or a point cloud; instanced curves and volumes do not.
Instance attributes (a color per instance) do not reach the material yet: an instance draws in its mesh's first material.
Points are spheres in their material in every shading mode; Solid does not give them Workbench's studio light yet.
The Node Editor's header has View only; its Select, Add and Node menus are reached by their keys (Shift A adds).
The sidebar's Group tab (the interface panels and their sockets' settings) is not shown yet.

title: Grease Pencil
summary: Draw and animate 2D strokes in the 3D Viewport with Blender's Grease Pencil, its brushes, modes, layers and onion skins, drawn by Babylon's GreasedLine.
expect: Drawing, editing, layers and animation run Blender's code; stroke ends are flat, some blend modes, masks, gradient and texture fills and shader effects draw differently.
limits: Stroke ends and corners are flat (GreasedLine has no round caps or joins); Dots and Squares strokes draw as lines.
A layer's opacity applies per stroke; Hard Light and Divide layers blend as Regular; layer masks do not mask.
Gradient and texture fills draw in their fill color, texture strokes in their stroke color; strokes are not lit.
Fills draw under their layer's strokes rather than interleaved stroke by stroke.
Shader effects (Blur, Shadow, Rim, ...) and Line Art's evaluation in a render are not drawn.
Line Art objects are added and evaluated in the module but are not checked against Blender's.
The paint cursor (the brush circle) and Bezier handles in Edit Mode are not drawn.

title: Hair Dynamics
summary: Hair curves grown by Generate Hair Curves and simulated by Blender's Hair Dynamics node group in a simulation zone.
expect: The simulation matches Blender frame by frame; a jump to a far frame simulates every frame up to it, and the Shader Editor does not show the hair's material.
limits: The Shader Editor does not show a Curves object's material; the Hair material is read from the .blend and drawn.
Simulating to a far frame plays every frame from the start, which takes a moment on slow devices.

title: Images and Image Textures
summary: Open, create, pack and save images with Blender's own readers and writers, view them in the Image Editor, and draw them on materials through the Image Texture node with Babylon's texture sampling.
expect: Images open, save, pack and draw on materials with Blender's readers; colors show with the Standard view, and Clip, Cubic, Box projection and UDIM sampling are simplified.
limits: The color management files (OpenColorIO config and LUTs) are fetched on first use, not at startup, until the module is built with exceptions.
The view transform (AgX, Filmic) is not applied to what Babylon draws; images display with the Standard view.
An Image Texture node's Clip extension clamps to the edge pixels, as Babylon's samplers have no border color.
Interpolation belongs to the image's GPU texture, so two nodes sampling one image with different interpolation share the last one.
Cubic and Smart interpolation sample linearly.
Box, Sphere and Tube projection of the Image Texture node are drawn as Flat.
UDIM images draw their first tile only.
Compressed GPU texture formats are not offered.
A file libpng cannot read or write stops the module: libpng reports errors by longjmp, which the module cannot catch yet.

title: Import and Export
summary: Bring scenes in and write them out with Blender's own importers and exporters (Wavefront OBJ, Stanford PLY, STL, FBX) and its default add-ons (glTF 2.0, FBX export, Motion Capture, SVG as Curves), through the browser's file dialogs with each format's options.
expect: OBJ, PLY, STL, FBX, glTF 2.0, BVH and SVG import and export with Blender's own code and options; the add-ons' entries wait a few seconds for Python the first time File opens, Alembic and USD are greyed out, and an export's extra files download.
limits: Alembic is greyed out until the module is built with C++ exceptions, which its reader relies on.
Universal Scene Description is greyed out; OpenUSD needs threads and run-time plugins the module does not have.
glTF 2.0, FBX export, Motion Capture (.bvh) and SVG as Curves are Blender's Python add-ons: opening File starts Python, and their entries stay greyed out until it has (a few seconds the first time).
glTF's Draco and meshoptimizer compression are not available; their libraries are native ones Bylonder does not build.
The file dialogs are the browser's; an export with several files (an OBJ's .mtl, a .gltf's .bin and textures) saves the first where you choose and downloads the others.
Imported color attributes are kept in Main; Solid shading's Attribute color and the Color Attribute node do not draw them yet.
The splash's Open from URL downloads only from servers that allow downloads from a web page (CORS); Blender's demo files are served from Bylonder's own copy for that reason.

title: Keyframe Animation
summary: Key an object's transform with I at two frames on the Timeline and play the animation with Space.
expect: Keying with I, the Timeline and playback work as in Blender; the demo itself is keyed from code, so the steps animate the Default Cube instead.
limits: The Keyframe Animation example keys a Babylon scene from code with the project SDK; the steps here key Blender's objects with I.

title: Link and Append
summary: Bring collections, objects, materials and any other data-block in from another .blend with File > Link and File > Append, browsing inside the file in Blender's own File Browser, and make linked data editable with library overrides.
expect: Link and Append run Blender's own code with all their options and browse the .blend in Blender's File Browser; the .blend comes from the browser's file dialog, the project keeps it in its libraries folder, and a .blend saved with File > Save As refers to it at /libraries/.
limits: The .blend to link from is chosen in the browser's file dialog first; Blender's File Browser then opens inside it, so its bookmarks and parent folders do not reach your computer's other files.

A library's path is /libraries/<name>.blend in Bylonder's file system, where the project keeps it; a .blend saved with File > Save As refers to it there, so Blender on your computer asks to relocate it.
The File Browser shows no previews of data-blocks: the module draws without a GPU, so files carry none it makes.

title: Mesh Modeling
summary: Model a mesh in Edit Mode with Blender's own tools, Loop Cut, Inset, Extrude, Bevel, Knife, Bisect and Spin, here shaping a rangefinder camera.
expect: Edit Mode's tools, their keys, modal options and gizmos are Blender's code and give Blender's result; picking elements under the pointer works as in X-ray, so hidden faces can be picked.
limits: Clicking selects as in X-ray, the element nearest the pointer whether or not a face in front hides it.
The example's model is built by its script with the bmesh operators these tools run (bmesh.ops.inset_region, bevel, spin, bisect_plane), not by recorded tool use.

title: Modifiers
summary: Add, edit and stack modifiers in Properties > Modifiers, here two Array modifiers that turn a cube into a floor of tiles.
expect: Blender's modifiers run Blender's code and give its result; modifier panels cut long labels short.
limits: The Array Modifiers example builds its arrays from code with Bylonder's Array (Nodes) modifier; the steps here use the Add Modifier menu.
Modifier panels lay out Blender's properties in a narrow column, so long labels are cut short.

title: Nonlinear Animation
summary: Layer and mix actions as strips on tracks in Blender's Nonlinear Animation editor, with push down, tweak mode, strip blending, influence and repeats, evaluated by Blender's animation system.
expect: Tracks, strips, push down, tweak mode and strip blending run Blender's code and evaluate as in Blender; sound strips and control curves are listed but not checked against Blender's drawing.
limits: Strips of sound clips and NLA control curves are listed but their sounds and curves are not checked against Blender's drawing.
Keyframe shapes on the action line are drawn without their extreme markers (the Dope Sheet's up and down arrows).

title: Particle Hair
summary: A hair particle system on a mesh, shaped with the Comb brush in Particle Edit Mode and set up in Properties > Particles.
expect: Hair systems, children and Particle Edit Mode's brushes run Blender's code; hair UV and color attributes are not drawn.
limits: Hair's UV and color attributes are not drawn.
Overlays of hair have no selection ids, clipping or Blender's line anti-aliasing.

title: Preferences
summary: Blender's Preferences editor with all of its sections and settings, kept in this browser, with laptop input (Emulate 3 Button Mouse, Emulate Numpad, trackpad gestures), Blender's keymaps to edit, and its themes on the interface.
expect: Input, navigation, keymaps and themes work and are kept in this browser; settings a browser cannot honor (NDOF, file paths, viewport quality, add-on installs) are greyed out.
limits: NDOF devices are greyed out: Bylonder is built without NDOF input, so the Gamepad API is not read.
Auto Depth has no depth buffer to read in the module; navigation centers as without it.
Interface settings the page draws itself (Line Width, fonts, pie menu timing, tooltips' Python) are greyed out until the page's interface follows them.
Viewport quality settings (Anti-Aliasing, Texture Limit, Anisotropic Filtering, Clip Alpha) and Studio Lights are shown greyed out; Babylon's drawing does not take them yet.
Theme colors that no design token stands for are greyed out. Reset to Default Theme gives Blender Dark; the theme presets menu (Blender Light) does not load its XML yet.
Add-ons lists every add-on Blender 5.2 ships; only Bylonder's own and the Pose Library run in the app, the others are greyed out as not included. Installing add-ons from disk or online is greyed out.
The Keymap lists operators Bylonder runs its own way as unavailable, as Blender lists an operator it lacks; their keys still work.
The Mouse panel's labels are cut short at the window's default width.
File Paths are greyed out: projects and their files live in the browser.

title: Python Scripts, Console and Add-ons
summary: Run Python scripts, type in the Python Console and install add-ons, with Blender's own bpy and numpy in CPython 3.13.
expect: Scripts, the Python Console and add-ons and extensions run on Blender's own bpy and numpy as in Blender once Python has loaded (a few seconds the first time); no threads, network or gpu module, and the interface itself stays on the app's own drawing.
limits: One thread: threading starts no thread and multiprocessing does not run.
No network from Python (urllib, pip, the online extension repositories), and no ctypes.
The gpu module is not built, so draw handlers that draw with GPU shaders draw nothing.
The shipped interface stays on the transpiled tree; a function added to one of its menus or panels draws before or after its own items.

title: Rendering
summary: Light a scene with Blender's lights and world and render it as EEVEE does, in Rendered shading and with Render Image, through Blender's camera.
expect: Lights, shadows, the world's color, glass and anti-aliasing render close to EEVEE from Blender's own settings; reflections and refraction see only the world, not the room around them.
limits: Shadows are filtered by a fixed amount, as EEVEE's filter radius; a light's Angle or Radius widens its highlights but does not soften its shadows' edges.
Reflections and refraction show the world's color only; EEVEE's light probes (sphere, plane, volume) and screen space reflections are not drawn, so glass and metal do not reflect the room.
The world lights by its color or an environment image; a node tree on the world beyond the Background shader is not evaluated.
Glass refracts the world behind it, not the objects; a Transparent BSDF mixed in lets the objects through.
AgX and Filmic map to Babylon's filmic tone mapping, not Blender's curves, so colors differ from Blender under those view transforms; Standard matches.
The 3D Viewport's camera view frames tighter than the camera when the viewport's aspect differs from the render's; Render Image frames as Blender does.

title: Rigging and Posing
summary: Pose an armature's bones in Pose Mode, select them with clicks, boxes, circles, lassos and L, key the pose with I, organize bones with bone collections and constraints, keep poses in the pose library's asset shelf, and paint a mesh's weights.
expect: Posing, selecting, keying, bone collections, constraints, weight paint and the pose library work as in Blender; bone selection ignores depth and pose assets have no preview.
limits: Bone selection does not test depth against the scene's meshes: a box also selects bones behind them, as in X-ray.
Pose assets have no preview image (Blender renders it on the GPU); a tile shows the pose's name.
Create Pose Asset saves into the Current File only; there is no User Library on disk.
The asset shelf's tiles have no hover highlight or tooltip, and the shelf does not scroll past the rows it shows.
Weight Paint's Show Wire is not drawn.
Bylonder's own meshes get vertex groups only from Blender's operators (With Automatic Weights); meshes read from a .blend keep theirs.
Selecting the armature in Object Mode outlines its child mesh too.

title: Sculpting
summary: Sculpt a mesh in Sculpt Mode with Blender's brushes, Grab, Draw, Crease, Inflate and Smooth, each stroke one undo step, here on a ceramic owl.
expect: Sculpt Mode, its brushes, their keys and strokes are Blender's code and move the mesh as Blender's do; dynamic topology and multiresolution sculpting are not set up in the steps.
limits: The owl's starting form is made by its script with brush-like falloffs (grab, draw, inflate and crease around points and along lines), not by recorded strokes.
Brushes are picked by their keys (V, G, C, Shift C, I, S); the brush asset shelf is not shown.

title: Shader Nodes
summary: Build a material from Blender's shader nodes in the Shader Editor, here a glowing lava on a sphere displaced by a Clouds texture.
expect: 76 of Blender's shader nodes run; textures, converters and inputs run Blender's GLSL and match EEVEE pixel for pixel, while shaders are Babylon's PBR lighting, close to EEVEE but not equal; lights cast hard-edged shadows (area lights none); Material Preview uses Babylon's studio light.
limits: Material Preview lights the scene with Babylon's studio environment, not Blender's forest.exr.
Bump takes the height's screen derivatives (Blender's fast path), not the height again at offset points.
Principled BSDF's sockets are one list, without Blender's collapsible panels.
The Texture tab's preview is empty.

A material's closures are lit as EEVEE's closure bins: the base (diffuse, Principled, refraction) once and up to two Glossy, Metallic or Anisotropic BSDFs each on its own; closures that share a bin are merged into one set of parameters (their colors, roughness, IOR and normals as they weigh), where EEVEE picks one of them per sample.
Glossy, Metallic and Anisotropic BSDF draw without their distribution choice, anisotropy, F82 tint or thin film.
Sheen draws as a diffuse closure of its color, as EEVEE does; Subsurface Scattering and Translucent draw as diffuse, without scattering or light from behind.

A sun's angle and a light's soft size widen its highlights as Babylon widens them (the surface's roughness plus the radius over the distance), not by EEVEE's integration over the light's disk, and cast no soft shadows.
A world color lights as EEVEE's world probe; an environment image lights as Babylon's environment, filtered as Babylon filters it, not as EEVEE's sphere probe.
Glass and Refraction BSDF refract the world only, not the objects behind them (Glass, sphere 18, mean dE 2.1, max 3).

Render Image takes 16 samples by default where EEVEE's render takes 64, filtered as EEVEE's film filters them (Blackman-Harris, 1.5 pixels); the film costs about 19 ms a frame on a software renderer (gallery viewport, 101 to 120 ms). The film keeps no transparency: a render's background is opaque.
Blender's view transforms other than Standard are approximated by Babylon's tone mapping.

Shadows have hard edges: a sun's angle and a light's soft size do not soften them yet (Shader Node Gallery floor tiles 21 to 24, mean dE 2.4 to 5.9, 99th percentile 18 to 48 at the edges). A light's shadow map (2048 texels a side, percentage closer filtered) covers every object that casts into it at once, so over a large scene shadows are coarser than EEVEE's virtual shadow maps. Area lights cast no shadows: Babylon's rectangular area light takes no shadow generator. A shadow map costs about 9 ms a frame at 2048 on a software renderer.
Material Preview lays blended surfaces over what is behind them in display space; Rendered shading and Render Image blend in scene linear, as EEVEE does.
A Transparent BSDF's color lets through its average, not each channel; Holdout draws black, not a hole in the film.
Light Path takes every ray as a camera ray; Ambient Occlusion finds no occlusion; Shader to RGB does not run.
Normal Map and Tangent read Blender's tangents of the active UV map; for another UV map, or a mesh Blender does not draw, they take the tangent from the UV map's screen derivatives.
Attribute, Color Attribute and a named UV Map read the attributes of meshes Blender draws, not of Babylon's own meshes.
Object Info's Material Index is 0; Geometry's Parametric and Random Per Island are 0.
Curves nodes draw the curves a file holds; the node has no curve widget to edit them.
Material Output's Displacement is not applied; a texture node's legacy texture mapping is ignored.
With EEVEE Parity off (Properties > Render), lobes are lit as one and the view direction is Babylon's eye, as plain Babylon PBR does.

File > Export writes a material of Blender's nodes as Babylon's own blocks, its Blender nodes one CustomBlock of their code: their values, the drawn object's color, index and texture space are fixed at export, and a color ramp's table is 8 bits.

The export's EEVEE Parity lights a second reflection lobe as Babylon's clearcoat, a dielectric whose strength follows the lobe's color, not as EEVEE's lobe; exported Principled-only materials (PBRMaterial) keep Babylon's view direction through an orthographic camera.
Not run yet: Wireframe, Point Info, Particle Info, the volume nodes, Script, Sky, Environment and IES textures, Toon BSDF, Specular BSDF, Ray Portal, Raycast, AOV Output and node groups.

title: Shape Keys
summary: Shape a mesh with Blender's shape keys, their values, ranges, vertex groups, relative keys, pinning and locks, edit a key in Edit Mode and key its value, drawn as Blender evaluates them or blended by Babylon's morph targets on the GPU.
expect: Shape keys, their values, ranges, pinning and Edit Mode work as in Blender; on Babylon (mapped) shading differs slightly between keys and only relative keys on unmodified meshes blend on the GPU.
limits: Babylon (mapped) blends each key's own normals linearly; Blender recomputes the normals of the blended positions, so shading differs slightly between keys.
Babylon (mapped) blends relative keys only, on a mesh with no modifier shown in the viewport; absolute keys (Relative off) and meshes with modifiers evaluate as Blender.

On Babylon (mapped) Blender's animation system still evaluates the keys into the mesh each frame (about 4 ms on 32k vertices), though nothing reads that mesh; the depsgraph has no hook to evaluate it only when read.

title: Spreadsheet
summary: Blender's Spreadsheet editor, listing the active object's evaluated or original geometry by component and domain, with its attributes as columns.
expect: Components, domains and evaluated or original data list as in Blender; the sidebar's row filters are missing and columns cannot be resized or reordered.
limits: The sidebar (N) with its row filters is not shown yet, and columns are not resized or reordered by dragging.
Selection filtering of rows in Edit Mode follows Blender's code but is not checked against Blender yet.

title: Texture Paint and Vertex Paint
summary: Paint an object's image texture in the 3D Viewport or the Image Editor with Blender's brushes and projection painting, and paint its color attribute in Vertex Paint Mode, one undo step per stroke.
expect: Painting in the 3D Viewport, the Image Editor and Vertex Paint runs Blender's brushes; colors show with the Standard view, and brush textures are not drawn in the cursor.
limits: The color management's view transform (AgX, Filmic) is not applied to what Babylon draws; images display with the Standard view.
Brush textures and masks (Texture and Texture Mask panels) are not drawn in the brush cursor.
Clone and Smear brushes paint only within one image; Clone from another image's UV map is not checked.

title: Touch and Pen
summary: Blender's own screens, keymaps and operators on large phones and tablets, with gestures for navigation, press and hold for tooltips and right clicks, pinch to scale the interface, drawers for areas that do not fit and a touch bar for keys.
expect: Blender's screens, menus, tools and context menus work by touch on a large phone or a tablet; the UI stays dense (pinch over it to scale it); a dragged value shows above the finger with soft Shift and Ctrl; area edges and headers take a long press; a one row touch bar gives modifier keys, a keys pie and a keyboard, with tappable bubbles while a transform runs; hover needs a pen.
limits: Shortcut bubbles show for the 3D Viewport's modal operators (transforms, Extrude); the 2D editors' (Graph Editor, Dope Sheet, Outliner) do not show them yet.
The quick keys pie's slots are fixed per mode; pinning or replacing a slot is not here yet.
Blender's pies (Z shading, accent grave views) open as menus, not drawn as pies.
An area carried by its header swaps with the area it is dropped on; docking it at another area's edge is not here yet.
Panels do not reorder by a hold and drag on their header.
Hover without a press (tool previews, Knife and Poly Build preselection) needs a pen; a finger has no hover, and the touch bar has no pointer mode yet.
Twisting two fingers does nothing; three fingers orbit.

title: UV Editing
summary: Unwrap a mesh with UV > Unwrap, Smart UV Project or Project from View, mark seams, and select, move, pin, stitch and pack its UVs in the UV Editor over the image they map.
expect: Unwrapping and UV editing run Blender's operators; UV Sculpt has no brush cursor and Display Stretch is not drawn.
limits: UV Sculpt tools are not drawn with a brush cursor.
The UV Editor's stretch display (Overlays, Display Stretch) is not drawn.

title: Vertex and Weight Paint
summary: Paint a mesh's color attribute in Vertex Paint and a vertex group's weights in Weight Paint, here the markings of two koi and the part of them a modifier swings.
expect: Vertex Paint and Weight Paint, their brushes, strokes and overlays are Blender's code and paint as Blender does, one undo step per stroke; a material shows a color attribute through the Color Attribute node.
limits: The example's markings and weights are written by its script from noise and the length of the fish, not painted by recorded strokes.
